evidence_items.explanation: The January conference paper reports inconsistencies involving adjective–noun composition in language embeddings. It also allows a mismatch between the linguistic theory and the representation as an explanation, so it does not establish the full claim about contemporary conversational models.

Controlled experiments find successful hierarchical generalization with language-model training across five tasks, although performance varies across tasks and training seeds. This qualifies any suggestion that transformers cannot learn structure, but predates the target window and does not establish broad reliability in contemporary deployed models.

unresolved_gaps: No independent evaluation retrieved here matches the cited study’s phenomena, contemporary model scope, and target period closely enough to settle the full proposition.
The semantic evidence concerns embeddings rather than a representative set of current general-purpose models.
The post does not define the frequency or reliability threshold needed to distinguish recurring limitations from ordinary occasional error.
